device.model: UR with Robotiq Hand-E in the gz-sim empty world
device.name: cambel ur_gripper_gz Hand-E gz-sim bringup

facts.text: README.md states ROS 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04 with Gazebo Harmonic (gz-sim 8), and points ROS 1 Noetic or Melodic with Gazebo Classic at the noetic-devel branch.
README.md says mimic joints need bullet-featherstone and that both gripper launches pass --physics-engine gz-physics-bullet-featherstone-plugin.
README.md says the Robotiq real-hardware driver (robotiq_control / pymodbus) is deferred.
LICENSE line 1 is The MIT License (MIT).
ur_gripper_gz/package.xml declares license BSD and build tool ament_cmake.
ur_gripper_gz/package.xml depends on ros_gz_bridge and ros_gz_sim.
ur_gz_control.launch.py starts a ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge with the argument /clock@rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock[gz.msgs.Clock.
ur_gz_control.launch.py starts ur_control's active_gripper_publisher with gripper robotiq_hande.
ur_gz_control.launch.py builds gz_args containing empty.sdf, -r and gz-physics-bullet-featherstone-plugin, and includes ros_gz_sim's gz_sim.launch.py.
ur_gz_control.launch.py spawns the model with -name set to the ur_type launch argument.
ur_gz_control.launch.py starts a controller_manager spawner named joint_state_broadcaster.
ur_gz_control.launch.py starts a controller_manager spawner named scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.
ur_gz_control.launch.py spawns forward_velocity_controller and cartesian_compliance_controller with --inactive.
ur_gz_control.launch.py spawns gripper_controller when load_gripper is true.
ur_gz_control.launch.py defaults ur_type to ur3e, describes that argument as including ur3, and defaults load_gripper to true.

ur_gz_control.launch.py registers OnProcessExit so spawn_entity's exit starts jsb_spawner, jsb_spawner's exit starts fts_spawner and jtc_spawner, and jtc_spawner's exit starts fvc_spawner, compliance_spawner and gripper_spawner.
force_torque_sensor_broadcaster is passed with -c and /controller_manager.
ur_gz_controllers.yaml says the trajectory controller is named scaled_joint_trajectory_controller so ur_control's Arm drives the simulated robot unchanged.
ur_gz_controllers.yaml sets controller_manager update_rate 500 and use_sim_time true, and sets joint_state_broadcaster's type to joint_state_broadcaster/JointStateBroadcaster.
ur_gz_controllers.yaml sets scaled_joint_trajectory_controller's type to joint_trajectory_controller/JointTrajectoryController.
ur_gz_controllers.yaml sets gripper_controller's type to joint_trajectory_controller/JointTrajectoryController.

ur_gz_controllers.yaml lists shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint and wrist_3_joint for scaled_joint_trajectory_controller, with command interface position.
ur_gz_controllers.yaml sets stopped_velocity_tolerance 0.05 and goal_time 0.6 on scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.
constants.py sets JOINT_POSITION_TRAJECTORY_CONTROLLER and JOINT_VELOCITY_TRAJECTORY_CONTROLLER to scaled_joint_trajectory_controller and JOINT_STATE_SUBSCRIBER to joint_states.
constants.py names shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint and wrist_3_joint.
constants.py sets JOINT_ORDER to those six joint names.
controllers.py imports JointState from sensor_msgs.msg.
JointControllerBase creates a JointState subscription on the relative name joint_states with qos_profile_sensor_data.
If that subscription waits past the timeout, JointControllerBase subscribes again to a topic built as the namespace plus joint_states.
JointTrajectoryController defaults publisher_name to scaled_joint_trajectory_controller and builds the command topic as the namespace plus that name plus /joint_trajectory.
JointTrajectoryController.stop calls cancel_goal_async on the goal handle when one exists.
check_for_real_robot returns True without calling the wrapped function when use_real_robot is false.
URServices sets use_real_robot from the parameter use_real_robot with default False.
URServices creates a std_srvs.srv.Trigger client named stop on the namespace plus ur_hardware_interface/dashboard/stop.
ur_2f85_gz_control.launch.py also builds gz_args containing empty.sdf and -r.
ur_2f85_gz_control.launch.py defaults ur_type to ur5e.
SimulationRunner composes its transport namespace as /world/ followed by the world name.
SimulationRunner advertises the control service with OnWorldControl as its callback.
OnWorldControl copies the WorldControl request into a WorldControlState and calls OnWorldControlState.
OnWorldControlState appends the control to worldControls and sets the Boolean reply data to true.
ProcessWorldControl calls SetPaused with the pause flag of each queued control.
A queued control with multi_step greater than zero while paused adds the steps and calls SetPaused false.
SetPaused stores the pause state in currentInfo.paused.
UpdateSystems calls PreUpdate on each system from SystemsPreUpdate.
UserCommands::PreUpdate takes an unused UpdateInfo, copies pendingCmds and calls Execute on each command.
Step calls PublishStats.
Step calls ProcessMessages.
While paused the Run loop does not count a processed iteration; without a network manager it calls Step.
The statistics publisher comment says the GUI listens to these messages for confirmation that pause and play GUI requests were processed.
The statistics publisher on the stats topic is limited to 10 messages per second.
PublishStats copies currentInfo.paused into the WorldStatistics message.
UpdateCurrentInfo advances simTime and the iteration count only in the branch that requires the world not paused.
The Physics system steps the physics only when not paused.
examples/worlds/empty.sdf names its world empty.
examples/worlds/empty.sdf loads gz-sim-physics-system, gz-sim-user-commands-system, gz-sim-scene-broadcaster-system and gz-sim-contact-system.
examples/worlds/empty.sdf then declares a directional light named sun and a model named ground_plane.
The bridge maps ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld to a gz.msgs.WorldControl request with a gz.msgs.Boolean reply.
The ControlWorld response's success is the gz Boolean reply's data.
For a failed gz request the ControlWorld response's success is false.
The service bridge converts each ROS request and sends it with gz Request and a callback that sends the ROS response.
Node::Request with a callback requests a service using a non-blocking call.
The WorldStatistics conversion copies the gz header, sim_time, pause_time, real_time and paused into the ROS message.
ros_gz_interfaces WorldStatistics carries a header, sim_time, pause_time, real_time and the paused flag.
ControlWorld takes a WorldControl request and answers bool success.
WorldControl's fields include pause, step and multi_step.
The bridge README maps ros_gz_interfaces/msg/WorldStatistics to gz.msgs.WorldStatistics.
The bridge README maps the ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld service to gz.msgs.WorldControl and gz.msgs.Boolean.
The bridge README's service example starts parameter_bridge with /world/shapes/control@ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld.
Without a configured QoS profile the bridge's publisher QoS is KeepLast with the publisher queue size.
The bridge's publisher allows its deadline, depth, durability, history, liveliness and reliability QoS to be overridden.
The gz-sim 8 CMake project is gz-sim8 version 8.15.0.
The gz-sim changelog heading is Gazebo Sim 8.15.0 (2026-08-11).
The gz-sim CMake file finds gz-transport13.
ros_gz_bridge package.xml declares version 1.0.25.
ros_gz_bridge CHANGELOG.rst records 1.0.25 (2026-10-13).
ros_gz_sim package.xml depends on gz_sim_vendor.
The gz-transport 13 CMake project is gz-transport13 version 13.6.0.
The gz-transport changelog heading is Gazebo Transport 13.6.0 (2026-08-15).

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no physics step or state-hash replay; world statistics follow the wall clock

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers /joint_states and the world-control service and publishes /world/empty/stats while subscribed, and it runs no gz-sim, ros_gz bridge, controller_manager or ROS graph

joint name, position and velocity samples are placeholders, including the six JOINT_ORDER strings; the clone states no unit on the joint_states subscription, and the schema fixes neither a length nor a unit

the clone does not show a publisher of /joint_states: the launch starts a spawner named joint_state_broadcaster (ur_gz_control.launch.py:106-113) and the yaml sets that controller's type (ur_gz_controllers.yaml:11-12), and neither line is a topic literal; a withheld sample is a timeout, and this package does not claim that joint_states goes silent while the world is paused

JointControllerBase retries with a topic built from the namespace (controllers.py:71); this package serves the relative name on line 64, resolved as /joint_states, and a namespaced deployment that never publishes that name times out

the trajectory endpoint is assembled (controllers.py:381) and is not published; the launch still starts scaled_joint_trajectory_controller (ur_gz_control.launch.py:129-136), whose yaml name is the one ur_control's Arm uses (ur_gz_controllers.yaml:4-5)

the stop reply is true when the control is queued (SimulationRunner.cc:1375-1377); ControlWorld.srv:3 comments that success means the control was successful, and that comment is the ROS reply text; confirmation is the E2 paused flag, not the reply

Step calls PublishStats (SimulationRunner.cc:1023-1024) before ProcessMessages (:1063-1064), so the sample that applies a queued pause still reports the previous flag; the read-back discards the first sample; the fake uses the same order and a placeholder 100 ms statistics period

the e-stop endpoints exist only while the operator runs ros_gz parameter_bridge with the two arguments of operator_bridges; the served launch's only parameter_bridge argument is the clock (ur_gz_control.launch.py:65-68), which this package does not subscribe to; estop_latency_ms 1500 covers the control call (400 ms) and the read-back bound (600 ms)

freshness is arrival time; the bridged header is the gz header (ros_gz_interfaces.cpp:840); without a QoS profile the publisher QoS is KeepLast (bridge_config.cpp:274-279), so durability stays the default volatile and a late subscriber sees no history; the first sample is discarded and a burst restarts the count; an operator QoS override (factory.hpp:61-82) is not covered beyond that rule

the endpoints use world name empty from the companion empty.sdf (examples/worlds/empty.sdf:63) that the launch names as a file (ur_gz_control.launch.py:87-89); a different world name means the declared endpoints do not exist and the e-stop fails closed

the served launch is ur_gz_control.launch.py only; ur_2f85_gz_control.launch.py also passes empty.sdf and defaults ur_type to ur5e (line 105) and is not served; ur_gz_control defaults ur_type to ur3e (line 174), and ur3 is an argument; the spawn name is ur_type (line 102) and the world name stays empty
the paused flag holds only for the confirmation window of two fresh samples at least 40 ms apart within 600 ms; it is not a lasting measured standstill

empty.sdf's plugin block is physics, user-commands, scene-broadcaster and contact (lines 68-83), then the sun light (line 85) and ground_plane (line 99); this package cites no WorldControl GUI plugin in that file; the GUI note is the statistics-publisher comment (SimulationRunner.cc:800-805)

UserCommands::PreUpdate takes an unused UpdateInfo, copies pendingCmds and calls Execute on each command (UserCommands.cc:669-699); UpdateSystems calls PreUpdate (SimulationRunner.cc:662-684) from Step, which the paused Run loop still calls (:896-911), so a queued world edit is still executed while the world is paused

a queued control with multi_step greater than zero while paused calls SetPaused false (SimulationRunner.cc:1445-1452); the GUI play path and another client's pause-false ControlWorld resume the world outside this package

no unpause is offered: the pause retains trajectory targets, because JointTrajectoryController.stop only calls cancel_goal_async and does not wait (controllers.py:493-498), and SetPaused stores currentInfo.paused (SimulationRunner.cc:1290-1291) and does not send that cancel, so this package cannot show that an unpause clears a trajectory the launch's controller accepted; mhs.safety.reset releases the MHS latch and the world stays paused; operator recovery outside MHS, after that pending motion is cleared, is to use the GUI play control or a pause-false ControlWorld outside MHS

while the e-stop latch is held, mhs.command of x-cap.cambel.joint-states.v1 is refused with MHS.SAFETY.ESTOP_ENGAGED, because an extension id is not treated as a read; mhs.safety.reset releases that refusal and leaves the world paused

a hardware path exists and is not served: check_for_real_robot skips the wrapped call when use_real_robot is false (ur_services.py:16-24), the parameter defaults false (line 38), the dashboard stop client is a Trigger (line 51), and README.md:211 defers the Robotiq real-hardware driver; the noetic-devel branch (README.md:6-7) is not served; there is no hardware backend

the deployment's gz-sim, ros_gz and gz-transport must be the pinned 8.15.0, 1.0.25 and 13.6.0; LICENSE:1 is the MIT License and ur_gripper_gz/package.xml:14 says BSD; publish_review stays not_required

measures.description: Read one sensor_msgs/JointState sample from the relative joint_states subscription
measures.name: read_joint_states

operator_bridges.description: The world control service: the e-stop pause.
The world statistics, whose paused flag confirms the e-stop.

safe_state.description: World empty reports paused true only inside the confirmation window of two fresh stats samples 40 ms apart within 600 ms after the WorldControl pause; it is the paused flag, not a measured standstill, and it needs the operator bridges; the pause retains trajectory targets; UserCommands executes queued world edits; a multi_step control, the GUI or another client can resume the world; this package offers no unpause; recovery outside MHS follows after pending motion is cleared.
